label: Vibe fires seven hook events: pre_agent, post_agent, pre_tool, post_tool, notification, session_start and session_end.
strict is accepted only on pre_tool, post_tool and pre_agent, so a hook can block a tool call but not a notification or a session boundary.
A hook is TOML with name, type, command, match, timeout defaulting to 60 seconds, strict and description, drawn from six sources and speaking the vibe, claude_code or kimi_code protocol.
The claude_code hook protocol means an existing Claude Code hook configuration can be consumed as-is, which is the cheapest porting path for a guard set.

notification and session_end run in the background with output ignored, while session_start runs synchronously and its additional_context is added to the next user message, which waits for the hook; close waits at most five seconds.
Safety is two layers: SandboxConfig with type local or managed plus SandboxAccess none, files or full, and PermissionRule rows matching stable tool IDs by glob with a behaviour.

Vibe can host four of the seven DSH event classes: tools/pre-execute to pre_tool, tools/post-execute to post_tool, agent/created to session_start and agent/disposed to session_end; agent/pre-step, agent/turn-stopping and session/event compaction have no home.

The deny-capable guards spec-gate-enforce, env-secret-guard, overlay-guard, mcp-route-guard, dispatch-preflight-lint and git-message-gate all become strict pre_tool hooks, while completion-evidence and ask-surface-guard cannot be expressed.

Correction to iteration 4: the goal bridge is partial, not absent, because a session_start hook can return additional_context injected into the next user message through the builtin session_start_context pre_agent binding; what is missing is a goal object with lifecycle.
